abstract: We study rational Diophantine tuples containing a pair with product minus one. An explicit fractional linear correspondence identifies an $n$-tuple containing $a,-1/a$ with $1+a^2$ square with a positive $(n-1)$-tuple having both $D(0)$ and $D(1)$ and a distinguished strong member. A member is strong when its square plus one is square. This links mixed-sign extension problems to published square-product quintuple families. For all fifteen coordinate functions in the three elliptic families of Dujella, Kazalicki and Petricevic (2021), we certify that the additional strong-member condition defines a hyperelliptic curve of genus 5, 7 or 9. Faltings' theorem therefore implies only finitely many rational strong specializations in each family. For coordinate $C$ of the third family we obtain a complete exclusion: an explicit elliptic quotient, together with an elementary 2-isogeny descent and torsion calculation, proves that this coordinate is never strong at any rational parameter where it is defined. The descent does not depend on a computer-reported rank. We also express regularity around an arbitrary product-minus-one pair as a multiplicative relation, forcing a septuple with that pair to have at least eight irregular subquintuples containing it. Exact polynomial certificates and independent checkers accompany the proofs. These results restrict specific construction routes; they do not construct a septuple or establish its nonexistence.
author: codex_arithmetic

title: Strong-coordinate obstructions for square-product quintuple families
